rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest candidate: chunk 5 ("Feedback-loopable methodology...") line 55 opens "Amp published twice here, with different bylines and different shapes" — "here" is a same-chunk forward reference, resolved within the same slide by the two bolded sub-entries that immediately follow (line 58 **Feedback Loopable**, line 60 **Handoff**); a reader takes in the whole projected slide before moving on, so this isn't a dangling referent. Chunk 8 line 130's "the two curated security skills from M3" names the module directly rather than pointing at it by position, covered by the arc-earned spine-vocabulary carve-out. No never-named, vague-with-history, or re-chunk-stranded referent found elsewhere.

No chunk points at another file by position ("the opening lecture said..."). The only cross-reference to training structure is chunk 8 line 130, "the two curated security skills from M3 (`/access-control-analysis` and `/stride`)" — named by module label and by the skills' own names, not by position, which is exactly the pattern §2 asks for ("Name the source by title or by its claim"). Within-file sequential callbacks (Klaassen/Pocock/Yan/Cognition/Ronacher reused by name across chunks 3, 5, 9) are rule-1 territory and fine, not §2 violations.

Every chunk carries a self-sufficient claim. Shortest is chunk 0 (lines 1-4), which still states the walk's whole shape in one paragraph ("One named framework, three architectural stances, one move-catalogue, one counter-position, plus a worked-example case study... Seven entries; not a closed set.") — not a wait-state or a bare context-dependent bullet.

Checked all 10 headers against their chunk bodies. Tightest case: chunk 5's two-part header "Feedback-loopable methodology and shipped primitives, Sourcegraph Amp" (line 54) is answered by two distinct bolded entries in the body — Metcalf's methodology (line 58) and the Handoff feature (line 60) — so the compound header isn't overclaiming. No header found whose own chunk content contradicts it.

Checked each sub-item. No "Not X. Not Y. Z." construction (grep clean). Closest to an anaphora triple is line 95's "No marketplace, no Git-checked-in kit, no orchestrator over the skills" — three genuinely distinct concrete nouns (distribution / version control / composition), not a repeated subject-verb clause, so it isn't the banned epistrophe shape. No self-grading superlative in curriculum voice (line 81's "most important" is inside a direct Cherny quote, not our own praise). Line 46's "roughly 58%" carries no self-retraction. No abstraction-noun-stack phrasing found (grepped for candidate patterns, zero hits). No empty-leg verb triplet found.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Internal dialect never lands on a slide.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Grepped the body for the named dialect terms (surface, firing, compendium, forcing function, beat, mood, Connections) — one hit, chunk 6 line 79: "agent picks up the human's existing tool surface." Harm check: this reads as ordinary industry usage (attack surface / API surface), a sense an engineer parses instantly and unrelated in denotation to this repo's own "writing surface" jargon the rule's example targets. The dialect-smuggling harm (a term the room in the chair cannot parse) is absent here, so this stays a PASS rather than a REVISE.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Emphasis budget — bold is for handles, and go very lightly.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Chunk 8 ("Skill stacking system, Dino: the worked example", lines 104-134) carries 7 bolded handles across two separate bulleted lists — "Around those mechanisms:" (lines 117-119: **A single orchestrator**, **Phase-organised skill catalogue.**, **Design principles**) and "Distinctive moves stand out:" (lines 123-126: **Front-loaded read-only analysis.**, **Mandatory gates fire positionally**, **Re-invocation as control flow.**, **CLAUDE.md as half the system.**) — plus one inline bold at line 128 (**scales cross-repo**). Each span is individually a legitimate handle (≤5 words, names a coined design principle), and the file isn't a plain narrative slide, but this is well past "≤1 bolded element on most slides" and past even the "one handle per law" consolidation allowance, which contemplates a single enumerated set, not two separate lists totalling 7-8 marks on one projected chunk. Chunk 8 already carries a rule-14 "Slide size accepted" note acknowledging its density; no equivalent rule-9 accept-note covers the bold count.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Trim to the 2-3 strongest handles per list (or one per list) and let the rest read as plain prose/bullets, or add a maintainer accept-note if the density is deliberate for this reading-only page.
